BURSEVI:v4p126/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r1.claim: One reading assigns the afternoon edge of day to noon and afternoon prayers, and the night approaches to sunset and night prayers, covering all five daily prayers.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r1.anchor: الظهر والعصر لأن ما بعد الزوال عشى

BURSEVI:v4p126/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r2.claim: Another reading takes the day's ends as morning and sunset and night approaches as night prayer plus tahajjud, obligatory for the Prophet; it cites the night vigil command.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r2.anchor: وفسر بعضهم طرفي النهار بالصبح والمغرب وزلف الليل بالعشاء

BURSEVI:v4p126/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r3.claim: Other interpretations include witr according to Abū Ḥanīfa, or night prayer, witr, and tahajjud together, matching the plural ‘approaches.’
BURSEVI:v4p126/r3.anchor: أو الوتر على ما ذهب إليه أبو حنيفة أو مجموع العشاء والوتر والتهجد

BURSEVI:v4p126/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r4.claim: A similar passage is read as morning before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, and sunset and night prayers at night.

BURSEVI:v4p126/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r5.claim: Good deeds, especially the five prayers, erase consequences of minor sins rather than undoing sins already committed; prayers, Fridays, and Ramadans expiate between them when major sins are avoided.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r5.anchor: على الإطلاق لا سيما الصلوات الخمس

BURSEVI:v4p126/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r6.claim: Prayer also restrains people from committing sins, as another verse says it keeps one from indecency and wrongdoing.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r6.anchor: إن الصلوة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر

BURSEVI:v4p126/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r7.speaker: أبو اليسر الأنصاري
BURSEVI:v4p126/r7.claim: Abū al-Yusr was tempted by a woman buying dates; he drew her home, embraced and kissed her but stopped before intercourse when she warned him to fear God, then regretted it.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r7.anchor: أن أبا اليسر الأنصاري كان يبيع التمر فأتته امرأة

BURSEVI:v4p126/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
BURSEVI:v4p126/r8.claim: Abū al-Yusr confessed to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, who advised concealing the sin and repenting, but he could not keep silent and went to the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r8.anchor: فأتى أبا بكر رضي الله عنه فأخبره

BURSEVI:v4p126/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126/r9.claim: The Prophet told him to wait for God's command; after the afternoon prayer the verse came, and prayer expiated his act for everyone.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r9.anchor: فلما صلى صلاة العصر نزلت هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v4p126/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v4p126/r10.claim: The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river at one's door, which leaves no dirt behind.
BURSEVI:v4p126/r10.anchor: لو أن نهرا بباب أحدكم يغتسل منه كل يوم خمس مرات

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r1.claim: Sins are impurities and acts of obedience purify; ablution washes away sins with its drops, so some jurists considered used ablution cloth impure and disliked praying in it.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r1.anchor: أن الذنوب كلها نجاسات والطاعات مطهرات وبماء أعضاء الوضوء تتساقط الأوزار

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r2.claim: A report has God tell Moses that each drop of ablution water used by Aḥmad and his community earns a garden as broad as the sky.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r2.anchor: يتوضأ أحمد وأمته كما أمرتهم وأعطيهم بكل قطرة

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r3.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r3.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's Persian couplet praises prayer and devoted appeal purified by tears and heart's blood.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r3.anchor: خوشا نماز ونياز كسى كه ازسردرد بآب ديده

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r4.claim: The highest good deed is knowledge of God, following monotheism, and opposing the lower self; remembrance purifies souls and hearts, strengthens obedience, and defeats Satan's schemes.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r4.anchor: العلم بالله ، وطريقه التوحيد ، وخلاف هوى النفس

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r5.claim: When companions ask whether ‘There is no god but God’ is a good deed, the Prophet says it is the best of good deeds.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r5.anchor: لا إله إلا الله من الحسنات قال

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r6.claim: The verse signals constant remembrance, worship, and obedience by day and night, with time for human needs, daytime work, and sleep to restore tired faculties for worship.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r6.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى إدامة الذكر والطاعة والعبادة في الليل والنهار

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r7.claim: In the inward reading, light from good deeds, remembrance, and watchfulness at day edges and night approaches erases the darkness of time spent on bodily needs.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r7.anchor: أي أن أنوار الحسنات وهي الأعمال الصالحة والذكر والمراقبة

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r8.claim: The luminous spirit would be lost through attachment to the dark body unless sacred good works nurture it, lift it toward spirituality and divine unity, and dispel bodily darkness.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r8.anchor: تعلق الروح النوراني العلوي بالجسد الظلماني السفلي موجب لخسران الروح

BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r9.claim: He compares this nurture to a seed that would be lost unless water made one seed into seven hundred, with God multiplying further as He wills.
BURSEVI:v4p126#2/r9.anchor: كما أن إلقاء الحبة في الأرض موجب لخسران الحبة

QASHANI:11:114-115/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r1.claim: The five senses distract the heart with bodily forms and veil it from divine presence; five prayers close those sensory doors, open the heart to God, focus attention, and admit light.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r1.anchor: لما كانت الحواس الخمس شواغل تشغل القلب بما يرد عليه من الهيئات الجسمانية

QASHANI:11:114-115/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r2.claim: Prayer's incoming light removes the darkness and residue of sensory distractions, meaning that good deeds remove evil deeds.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله: { إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات } وقد ورد

QASHANI:11:114-115/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r3.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:11:114-115/r3.claim: A prophetic report says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r3.anchor: إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر

QASHANI:11:114-115/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r4.claim: Praying at both ends of the day lets gathered presence and light persist through other times and remove their fragmentation, sustaining continual prayer.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r4.anchor: لينسحب حكمها ببقاء الجمعية واستيلاء الهيئة النورية في أوله إلى سائر الأوقات

QASHANI:11:114-115/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r5.claim: Natural powers dominate at night, drawing the soul to bodily management and sleep and away from spiritual perception; wakefulness and prayer refine and illuminate them.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r5.anchor: لما كانت القوى الطبيعية المدبرة لأمر الغذاء سلطانها في الليل

QASHANI:11:114-115/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:114-115/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:114-115/r6.claim: These prayer times and removal of sins remind those who remember their state of clarity, gathered attention, intimacy, and spiritual taste.
QASHANI:11:114-115/r6.anchor: تذكير لمن يذكر حاله عند الحضور مع الله في الصفاء والجمعية

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r4.claim: Good deeds granted by God erase the servant’s sins; nearness, remorse, tears, and repentance are among the deeds that erase different faults.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r4.anchor: الحسنات ما يجود بها الحق ، والسيئات ما يذنبها العبد

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r5.claim: Seeking forgiveness erases both disobedience and persistence in sin; divine solicitude erases wrongdoing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r5.anchor: ويقال حسنات القربة تذهب بسيئات الزلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r6.claim: Kindness toward fellow believers erases resentment, and generosity erases the wrongs of servants.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r6.anchor: حسنات العفو عن الإخوان تذهب الحقد عليهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r7.claim: Good opinion erases their ill opinion of you; divine favor erases the belief that one’s obedience is self-earned.

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r8.claim: Truthfulness erases self-admiration, and sincerity erases ostentation.

QIRAAT-ER:11:114:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:114:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:114:7#1/r1.claim: The vowel shift from zulafan to zulufan changes the internal pattern of the plural without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:11:114:7#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: zulafan → zulufan (ḍamma on lām) — plural of zulfa with different internal vowel pattern

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recounts a man who struck a woman on her backside and asked the Prophet about expiation; after asking whether intercourse occurred, the Prophet waited for revelation, and this verse came down.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار ﴾ قال ضرب رجل على كفل امرأة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the two ends of the day as dawn and afternoon prayers, and the night approaches as Maghrib and Isha.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r2.anchor: قال معمر عن قتادة هي الصبح والعصر ﴿ وزلفا من الليل ﴾ قال هي المغرب والعشاء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r3.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies dawn, afternoon, Maghrib, and Isha; he explains the good deeds that erase sins as the prayers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار ﴾ قال صلاة الفجر وصلاة العصر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains both the erasing good deeds and the remaining righteous deeds as the five prayers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ﴿ إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ﴾ قال الصلوات الخمس والباقيات الصالحات الصلوات الخمس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r5.claim: A man confessed to kissing and fondling a woman without intercourse; the Prophet recited this passage, and, answering Muadh, said its lesson applies to everyone.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p313#3/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله إني أخذت امرأة في البستان

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r1.speaker: يحيى بن جعدة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r1.claim: A Companion found a woman by a pool, stopped after an arousal, repented to the Prophet, and was told to seek forgiveness and pray four units; the Prophet then recited the verse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r1.anchor: عن يحيى بن جعدة أن رجلا من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر امرأة وهو جالس مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r2.claim: A rigorous worshiper who made people despair of God's mercy was told after death that he deserved Hell and would now be made to despair of mercy.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن رجلا كان في الأمم الماضية يجتهد في العبادة ويشدد على نفسه ويقنط الناس من رحمة الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r3.claim: The Prophet said a mother bird entrusted herself and her chick to people out of mercy for her young, and God's mercy toward the believing servant is greater.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p315/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال كان الرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض أسفاره فأخذ رجل فرخ طائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r1.speaker: الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r1.claim: Al-Layth defines زلفة as a portion of the first part of night and gives زلف as its plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r1.anchor: الزلفة قال الليث: طائفة من أول الليل، والجمع الزلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r2.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r2.claim: Thaʿlab says زلف are the first hours of night and زلفة is singular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r2.anchor: وقال ثعلب: الزلف أول ساعات الليل، واحدها زلفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة، والأخفش، وابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r3.claim: They gloss زلف as the hours and periods of night, each hour being a زلفة; al-Ajjaj's verse illustrates the word's repeated plural form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة، والأخفش، وابن قتيبة، الزلف ساعات الليل وآناؤه، وكل ساعة زلفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r4.claim: زلفة derives from nearness and approach, as shown by the related forms meaning to bring near and draw close.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r4.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من الزلفى وهي القربة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says the verse was revealed after a man had relations with a non-maḥram woman short of intercourse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها ما في صحيح مسلم من حديث الرجل الذي عالج امرأة أجنبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.claim: Another account says the verse predated the incident and the Prophet applied it to that man; when asked whether it was only for him, he said it was for everyone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: نزلت قبل ذلك، واستعملها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في قصة هذا الرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.claim: Addressing the Prophet directly in commands to do good, while directing prohibitions to the community, is a mark of eloquence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.anchor: حيث كان بأفعال الخير توجه الخطاب إليه، وحيث كان النهي عن المحظورات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.claim: The commanded prayer is the obligatory prayer; إقامة means maintaining it continuously, performing it fully, or performing it at its best times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف أن المأمور بإقامتها هي الصلوات المكتوبة، وإقامتها دوامها، وقيل: أداؤها على تمامها، وقيل: فعلها في أفضل أوقاتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.claim: طرفي النهار is an adverbial accusative; because each طرف belongs to the thing it bounds, the apparent referents are dawn and afternoon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.anchor: فالذي يظهر أنهما الصبح والعصر، لأنهما طرفا النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.claim: The fasting rule that dawn belongs to daytime supports dawn as one boundary: deliberate eating or intercourse after dawn invalidates the fast and entails makeup and expiation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.anchor: على أن من أكل أو جامع بعد طلوع الفجر متعمدا أن يومه يوم فطر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.claim: They identify the two daytime prayers as dawn and ʿAṣr, and the night approaches as Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, leaving Ẓuhr outside this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.anchor: وممن قال: هما الصبح والعصر الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وقال: الزلف المغرب والعشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r8.claim: They assign the first boundary to dawn and the second to Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, with Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at night; the passage says dawn is not included in this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب: الطرف الأول الصبح، والثاني الظهر والعصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r9.claim: They identify the boundaries as dawn and Maghrib and the night prayer as ʿIshāʾ, excluding Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا: هما الصبح والمغرب، والزلف العشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r10.claim: A further view takes Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as the boundaries and dawn, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ as night prayers, apparently grouping them by recitation aloud or quietly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p221#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: هما الظهر والعصر، والزلف المغرب والعشاء والصبح، وكأن هذا القائل راعى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r1.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās’s dawn-and-Maghrib interpretation; Abū Ḥayyān objects that Maghrib belongs to night, so calling it a daytime boundary requires metaphor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r1.anchor: ورجح الطبري قول ابن عباس: وهو أن الطرفين هما الصبح والمغرب، ولا نجعل المغرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes dawn as the morning prayer, Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as afternoon prayers, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ as the night approaches.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: غدوة وعشية قال: وصلاة الغدوة الصبح، وصلاة العشية الظهر والعصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r3.claim: Calling the period after noon ʿashiyy does not make Ẓuhr a boundary, since the command names the day's two boundaries rather than morning and afternoon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r3.anchor: ولا يلزم من إطلاق العشي على ما بعد الزوال أن يكون الظهر طرفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r4.claim: The majority read zulafan with an open lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وزلفا بفتح اللام، وطلحة وعيسى البصرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r5.speaker: طلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r5.claim: These readers use a damma on the lām, as though the word were a singular noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r5.anchor: وطلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر: بضمها كأنه اسم مفرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r6.claim: They read the lām quiescent; a further transmission from them has zulfa on the fuʿlā pattern, a feminine singular meaning a station or degree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ومجاهد: بإسكانها، وروي عنهما: وزلفى على وزن فعلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r7.claim: The plural readings treat the word as successive stations or as a collective noun; zulafā is equivalent to one zalfa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r7.anchor: فزلف جمع كظلم، وزلف كبسر في بسر، وزلف كبسر في بسرة، فهما اسما جنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r8.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates the night approaches with the two daytime boundaries as another bounded period.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r8.anchor: والظاهر عطف وزلفا من الليل على طرفي النهار، عطف طرفا على طرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains zulaf as the part of the day near nightfall; another interpretation makes it night prayers of devotion and coordinates it with الصلاة instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقد ذكر هذه القراآت وهو ما يقرب من آخر النهار من الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r10.claim: Hasanāt can mean all good deeds, especially obligatory prayers and Ramadan fasting; sayyiʾāt in this reading means minor sins, as supported by the sound report about avoiding major sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r10.anchor: والظاهر عموم الحسنات من الصلوات المفروضة، وصيام رمضان، وما أشبههما من فرائض الإسلام. وخصوص السيئات وهي الصغائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r11.speaker: جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r11.claim: Most early interpreters identify the good deeds specifically as the five prayers; Mālik adopts this interpretation, and ʿUthmān illustrates it while performing ablution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r11.anchor: وذهب جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين: إلى أن الحسنات يراد بها الصلوات الخمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r12.claim: Mujāhid interprets the good deeds as the formulas of remembrance: glorifying and praising God, proclaiming his oneness and greatness, and declaring reliance on him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحسنات قول الرجل: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r13.claim: These interpretations should be understood as examples; the five prayers are the greatest deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r13.anchor: وينبغي أن يحمل هذا كله على جهة المثال في الحساب، ومن أجل أن الصلوات الخمس هي أعظم الأعمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r14.claim: Minor sins are erased only when one repents and does not persist in them, a position stated explicitly by the most discerning legal theorists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r14.anchor: والصغائر التي تذهب هي بشرط التوبة منها وعدم الإصرار عليها، وهذا نص حذاق الأصوليين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r15.claim: Erasing sins means expiating minor sins, not making past acts cease to have happened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r15.anchor: ومعنى إذهابها: تكفير الصغائر، والصغائر قد وجدت وأذهبت الحسنات ما كان يترتب عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r16.claim: Another explanation is that good deeds graciously help people leave sins rather than erase sins already committed, as prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r16.anchor: وقيل: المعنى إن فعل الحسنات يكون لطفا في ترك السيئات، لا أنها واقعة كقوله: إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r17.claim: The demonstrative ذلك most apparently points to the nearest command: establishing prayer at these times as a reminder for those who take heed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r17.anchor: والظاهر أن الإشارة قوله ذلك، إلى أقرب مذكور وهو قوله: أقم الصلاة أي إقامتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r18.claim: Other referents for ذلك are the news that good deeds erase sins, earlier commands and prohibitions, or the Qurʾān; al-Zamakhsharī gives the earlier counsel as his view and al-Ṭabarī points to this sūrah's commands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p222/r18.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى الإخبار بأن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات، فيكون في هذه الذكرى حضا على فعل الحسنات

AKHFASH:v1p391/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p391/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p391/r3.claim: The yāʾ in طرفي النهار is vocalized because it meets a following still consonant; still consonants are usually given kasra, as in صاحبي السجن.
AKHFASH:v1p391/r3.anchor: وقال {طرفي النهار} فحرك الياء لأنها ساكنة لقيها حرف ساكن

AKHFASH:v1p391/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p391/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p391/r4.claim: زلفا is a plural of زلفة, with زلفات and زلف also used as plural forms.
AKHFASH:v1p391/r4.anchor: وقال {وزلفا من الليل} لأنها جماعة تقول "زلفة" و"زلفات" و"زلف"

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r1.claim: Establish the prescribed prayers fully; other reported meanings are to maintain them regularly or perform them at the start of their times.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r1.anchor: أي المكتوبة ومعنى إقامتها أداؤها على تمامها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r2.claim: The two ends mean the beginning and end of the day. Zulf are hours near the day; al-Layth and Thaʿlab say the first part of night, while Abū ʿUbayda, al-Akhfash, and Ibn Qutayba say any night hour, supported by al-ʿAjjāj’s verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r3.claim: Zulf is coordinated with the two ends, and min al-layl qualifies it. End prayers are variously dawn and afternoon, dawn and sunset, or dawn then noon and afternoon; Abū Ḥayyān favors dawn and afternoon, while noon as an endpoint is questioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r3.anchor: وهو عطف على ( طرفي النهار ) و ( من الليل ) في موضع الصفة له

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r4.claim: Most identify the night prayers as sunset and evening; a report via al-Ḥasan from Ibn ʿAbbās specifies ʿatama. Another reading makes zulf night prayers drawing near to God, perhaps the Prophet’s night prayer or evening and witr.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156/r4.anchor: والمراد بصلاة الزلف عند الأكثر صلاة المغرب والعشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r1.claim: Ṭalḥa, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and Abū Jaʿfar read zuluf with a rounded lām; Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with a silent lām, and a variant has zulfa, a synonymous form.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر ( زلفا ) بضم اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r2.claim: Good deeds expiate sins and remove liability, not sins as entities; another view says their records are erased. The view that they prevent sinning is remote and contrary to reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r2.anchor: أي يكفرنها ويذهبن المؤاخذة عليها وإلا فنفس السيئات أعراض وجدت فانعدمت

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r3.claim: The apparent scope is obligatory and voluntary good deeds, though some restrict it to obligations. Reports about affirmation matching angels, fasting ʿArafa, and gratitude after eating or dressing support voluntary acts as expiators.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد من الحسنات ما يعم الصلوات المفروضة وغيرها من الطاعات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r4.speaker: أبو اليسر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r4.claim: The occasion is reported as Abū al-Yusr regretting he kissed a woman; after waiting for revelation, the Prophet said prayer atoned for it. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn al-Musayyib also transmit this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r4.anchor: أبا اليسر من الأنصار قبل امرأة ثم ندم فأتى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r5.claim: Those who identify good deeds as obligatory prayers likely cite one important instance in the general category; the occasion does not restrict the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p156#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن ذلك منهم إقتصار على بعض مهم من أفراد ذلك العام وسبب النزول لا يأبى العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r1.claim: Most take ‘sins’ as minor sins and say major sins require repentance, citing Muslim’s report through al-ʿAlāʾ that five prayers expiate the interval if major sins are avoided.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r1.anchor: والمراد بالسيآت عند الأكثرين الصغائر لأن الكبائر لا يكفرها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r2.speaker: البلقيني
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r2.claim: Al-Balqīnī says 4:31 concerns avoiding major sins throughout life, whereas the prayer report concerns each day; al-Samhūdī objects that lifelong avoidance entails daily prayer, then discusses multiple expiators retaining their rewards.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r2.anchor: وأجاب البلقيني بأن ذلك غير وارد لأن المراد بالآية أن تجتنبوا في جميع العمر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects a lifelong reading of 4:31: the reward for avoiding major sins at each time expiates minor sins committed then, as al-Qāḍī and al-Ghazālī support.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد من ذلك أن ثواب إجتناب الكبائر في كل وقت يكفر الصغائر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r4.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī says restraint expiates only when someone has ability and desire to commit a major sin; abstaining from incapacity or lack of desire does not earn that effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r4.anchor: إجتناب الكبيرة إنما يكفر الصغيرة إذا إجتنبها مع القدرة والإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r5.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r5.claim: Al-Nawawī says that when an expiatory act coincides with major sins but no minor sins, one may hope that the major sins are lightened.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p157/r5.anchor: أنه صادف فعل المكفر كبيرة أو كبائر ولم يصادف صغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī reconciles the evidence by making avoidance of major sins a limit on expiating all interval sins, not a condition for any expiation: prayers expiate minors and all interval sins when majors are avoided.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r1.anchor: ما اجتنبت الكبائر في الخبر ليس قيدا لأصل التكفير بل لشمول التكفير سائر الذنوب التي بين الصلوات الخمس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r2.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r2.claim: Ibn Ḥajar says avoiding major sins entails performing the five prayers, since abandoning prayer is major; al-Ālūsī says this argument merits examination.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r2.anchor: وعلى تقدير ورد السؤال فالتخلص عنه سهل وذلك لأنه لا يتم إجتناب الكبائر إلا بفعل الصلوات الخمس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r3.speaker: المحب الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r3.claim: Al-Muḥibb al-Ṭabarī records two views: the majority make avoidance of major sins a condition; another treats it as an exception, so expiation excludes major sins, which he calls stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r3.anchor: إختلف العلماء في أمر تكفير الصغائر بالعبادات هل هو مشروط بإجتناب الكبائر على قولين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r4.speaker: الزركشي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r4.claim: Al-Zarkashī reports disagreement over requiring repentance for expiation; al-Baḥr says the requirement is explicit among rigorous legal theorists.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r4.anchor: ذكر الزركشي أنهم إختلفوا في أن التكفير هل يشترط فيه التوبة أم لا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r5.speaker: السبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r5.claim: Al-Subkī says acceptance of repentance from unbelief is certain by grace, but acceptance for sins is disputed; other authorities differ over whether its expiation is presumptive or certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r5.anchor: والمنقول عن السبكي أنه قال : إن قبول التوبة عن الكفر مقطوع به تفضلا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r6.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r6.claim: Al-Nasafī, Ṣadr al-Sharīʿa, and other Sunni scholars allow punishment for minor sins even when major sins are avoided, citing 4:48 and 18:49; the Muʿtazila deny it based on 4:31, which may concern unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p158/r6.anchor: أن العقاب على الصغائر جائز الوقوع سواء إجتنب مرتكبها الكبائر أم لا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r1.speaker: صاحب الذخائر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r1.claim: The author of al-Dhakhāʾir argues that some good deeds expiate minor and major sins, citing reports promising forgiveness of past and future sins; Ibn al-Mundhir leans this way.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r1.anchor: وذهب صاحب الذخائر إلى أن من الحسنات ما يكفر الصغائر والكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r2.claim: Critics call broad expiation ignorance and agreement with the Murjiʾa, arguing repentance would be pointless; al-Ālūsī replies that expiation differs from Murjiʾism and repentance remains obligatory for new and recurring delay sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r2.anchor: إن الكبائر والصغائر تكفرها الطهارة والصلاة لظاهر الأحاديث

ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r3.claim: Past expiation does not remove the ongoing duty to repent, just as a sleeper whose prayer time passed must still make it up; the Abū Hurayra report is specific and cannot be extended by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r3.anchor: ولا يلزم من تكفير الله تعالى ذنوب عبده سقوط التكليف بالتوبة التي كلف بها تكليفا مستمرا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r4.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r4.claim: Repentance for minor sins is obligatory according to al-Ashʿarī, with al-Juwaynī and al-Anṣārī reporting consensus; ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām says delay incurs renewed sin over time.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p159/r4.anchor: التوبة من الصغائر واجبة على ما نقل عن الأشعري وحكى إمام الحرمين وتلميذه الأنصاري الإجماع عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r1.claim: The reminder benefits those who heed admonition, singled out because they are the ones who benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r1.anchor: أي عظة للمتعظين وخصهم بالذكر لأنهم المنتفعون بها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says ‘that’ refers to the counsel about uprightness, avoiding tyranny and inclination toward wrongdoers, and establishing prayer at the named times; Abū Ḥayyān prefers prayer alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r2.anchor: والإشارة إلى ما تقدم من الوصية بالإستقامة والنهي عن الطغيان والركون إلى الذين ظلموا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r3.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the reference as the sūrah’s commands and prohibitions; others identify the Qurʾān, or prayer and repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى الأوامر والنواهي في هذه السورة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r1.claim: One reading of the day’s two ends is dawn and evening, meaning the dawn and sunset prayers; Mujahid includes dawn, noon, and afternoon, with sunset and night prayers as the night’s portions.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r2.claim: Muqatil assigns dawn and noon prayer to one end of the day, afternoon and sunset to the other, and night prayer to the night’s portions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: صلاة الفجر والظهر طرف، وصلاة العصر والمغرب طرف، وزلفا من الليل، يعني: صلاة العشاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r3.claim: Al-Hasan takes the two ends as dawn and afternoon prayers, and the night portions as sunset and night prayers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: طرفا النهار. الصبح والعصر، وزلفا من الليل: المغرب والعشاء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the ends as morning and evening, meaning dawn and sunset prayers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: طرفا النهار الغداة والعشي، يعني صلاة الصبح والمغرب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r5.claim: The night portions are its hours, each called a zulfa; Abu Jafar reads زلفا with a damma on the lam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p204/r5.anchor: ساعاته واحدتها زلفة. وقرأ أبو جعفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205/r1.claim: “That” points either to what was just described or to the Quran; it is a reminder for those who remember.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p205/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {ذلك} أي: ذلك الذي ذكرنا. وقيل: هو إشارة إلى القرآن، {ذكرى} عظة {للذاكرين} أي لمن ذكره.

NAHHAS:v2p306/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p306/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p306/r2.claim: طرفي النهار is a time adverb; readings vary on زلفا; حسنات may mean prayers, while repentance removes sins.
NAHHAS:v2p306/r2.anchor: نصب على الظرف وحذفت النون للإضافة وكسرت الياء لالتقاء الساكنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r1.claim: The two ends of the day are morning and evening: dawn prayer is the first prayer near daytime, while the evening prayer may mean afternoon or noon and afternoon; the nearby night prayers are sunset and night prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r1.anchor: غدوة وعشية وانتصابه على الظرف لأنه مضاف إليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r2.claim: Zulafan are hours near the day, a plural of zulfa; readings include zuluf, zuluf, and zulfa, with the latter meaning one near period.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r2.anchor: وساعات منه قريبة من النهار، فإنه من أزلفه إذا قربه وهو جمع زلفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r3.claim: Good deeds erase sins, and prayer from one prayer to the next expiates what lies between them if major sins are avoided.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r3.anchor:
يكفرنها. وفي الحديث
" إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر "

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r4.speaker: رجل
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r4.claim: A man told the Prophet that he had done something with a woman but had not had intercourse; this verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r4.anchor: أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني قد أصبت من امرأة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r5.claim: The phrase 'that is a reminder' may refer to steadfastness and what follows or to the Qur'an; it is an admonition for those who take heed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:114/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله { فاستقم } وما بعده وقيل إلى القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r8.claim: Prayer is the highest expiation for the weakness and lassitude that cause minor sins, and after faith it is the best act of worship and the broadest aid to uprightness.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r8.anchor: وذلك يدل على أنها بعد الإيمان أفضل العبادات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r9.claim: The two ends of the day mean morning and afternoon prayers, as prescribed in Mecca before the Night Journey; noon may also be intended as the second end.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r9.anchor: بالصبح والعصر كما كان مفروضا بمكة في أول الأمر قبل الإسراء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r10.claim: Zulaf are groups, stages, or periods of night; they may mean the early obligatory night vigil, or Maghrib and Isha with witr or night vigil.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r10.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد به التهجد , فقد كان مفروضا في أول الإسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r11.claim: All acts of obedience grounded in faith, including prayer, erase minor sins; major sins require repentance, while merely avoiding them expiates only with a sound intention.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p585/r11.anchor: الطاعات كلها الصلاة وغيرها المبنية على أساس الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that after a man confessed to kissing a woman, the Prophet recited this verse and said it applies to whoever among his community acts by it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أم رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas regards the verse as belonging to the Meccan and Medinan portions of the surah; the cited report supports that view.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r2.anchor: وهذا الحديث يؤيد قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن هذه الآية من هذه السورة المكية المدنية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r3.claim: The preceding exhortation, warning, consolation, and instruction in the remedy for misery form a great reminder for those able to attend, reflect clearly, and understand deeply.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587/r3.anchor: الأمر العالي الرتبة الذي تقدم من الترغيب والترهيب والتسلية وتعليم الداء والدواء

DURR-FULL:v4p480/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the two ends of the day as sunset and dawn prayers, and the night intervals as the late evening prayer.
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: صلاة المغرب والغداة {وزلفا من الليل}

DURR-FULL:v4p480/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r9.claim: Hasan identifies the ends of the day as dawn and afternoon prayers, and the night intervals as sunset and night prayers; he says the Prophet called the latter the two night intervals.
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: الفجر والعصر {وزلفا من الليل} قال: هما زلفتان

DURR-FULL:v4p480/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies the day prayers as dawn, noon, and afternoon, and the night intervals as sunset and night prayers.
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: صلاة الفجر وصلاتي العشاء يعني الظهر والعصر

DURR-FULL:v4p480/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r11.claim: Mujahid also glosses the night intervals as successive hours, referring to the late night prayer.
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وزلفا من الليل} قال: ساعة بعد ساعة يعني صلاة العشاء الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v4p480/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas preferred delaying the night prayer and would cite “and at intervals of the night.”
DURR-FULL:v4p480/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يستحب تأخير العشاء ويقرأ {وزلفا من الليل}

DURR-FULL:v4p482/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r1.claim: The Prophet applies the prayer instruction to everyone, not only the man in the preceding account.
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r1.anchor: فقرأ عليه {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} الآية فقال معاذ بن جبل: يا رسول الله أله وحده أم للناس كافة

DURR-FULL:v4p482/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r2.speaker: أبو اليسر
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r2.claim: Abu al-Yusr says he kissed a woman who came to buy dates, confessed to Abu Bakr and Umar, then told the Prophet, who reproached him; the verse was revealed and applied generally.
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r2.anchor: عن أبي اليسر قال أتتني امرأة تبتاع تمرا فقلت: إن في البيت تمرا أطيب منه

DURR-FULL:v4p482/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r3.claim: A man who asked for punishment was told after praying with the Prophet that he was cleansed of his sin like a newborn; the verse was revealed then.
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله أقم في حد الله

DURR-FULL:v4p482/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r4.claim: Mu'adh reports a man asking about intimate contact with a woman short of intercourse; the verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v4p482/r4.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال: رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ما ترى في رجل لقي امرأة لا يعرفها

DURR-FULL:v4p483/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r1.claim: In Mu'adh's account, the Prophet prescribed careful ablution and prayer and said the instruction applies generally to believers.
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r1.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توضأ وضوءا حسنا ثم قم فصل قال معاذ: فقلت يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p483/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r2.claim: A man confessed to touching a woman whose husband was away on campaign; Umar insisted the revealed prayer instruction applied to all believers, and the Prophet agreed.
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن امرأة جاءت تبايعني

DURR-FULL:v4p483/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r3.claim: Another report says a man confessed to having done something with a woman short of intercourse, after which the prayer verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني نلت من امرأة

DURR-FULL:v4p483/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r4.claim: A man who desired a woman tried to approach her while she bathed in a pool, but his organ became limp; the Prophet prescribed four prayer cycles, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رجلا كان يحب امرأة فاستأذن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حاجة

DURR-FULL:v4p483/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r5.speaker: بريدة
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r5.claim: A date seller led an Anṣari woman home and pressured her, then regretted sexual contact short of intercourse; the Prophet prayed with him, explained the five prayers named in the verse, and said its cleansing applies to everyone.
DURR-FULL:v4p483/r5.anchor: عن بريدة قال جاءت امرأة من الأنصار إلى رجل يبيع التمر بالمدينة وكانت امرأة حسناء جميلة

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r1.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r1.claim: A man kissed a woman who came to buy flour and regretted it; the verse was revealed, and Ata says it refers to the obligatory prayers.
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح قال: أقبلت امرأة حتى جاءت إنسانا يبيع الدقيق لتبتاع منه

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says Ibn Muqib confessed to touching a woman short of intercourse; the Prophet waited for guidance, then recited the verse to him.
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال جاء فلان بن مقيب رجل من الأنصار فقال: يا رسول الله دخلت على امرأة

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r3.speaker: سليمان التيمي
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r3.claim: A man who struck a woman's backside asked Abu Bakr, Umar, and the Prophet about expiation; none knew until the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r3.anchor: عن سليمان التيمي قال: ضرب رجل على كفل امرأة ثم أتى إلى أبي بكر وعمر فسألهما عن كفارة ذلك

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r4.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r4.claim: A man from Banu Tamim kissed and touched a woman, then consulted the caliphs and Prophet; the verse was revealed, and his continued remembrance explains “a reminder for those who remember.”
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r4.anchor: عن يزيد بن رومان أن رجلا من بني تميم دخلت عليه امرأة فقبلها ووضع يده على دبرها

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r5.speaker: يحيى بن جعدة
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r5.claim: A man attempted sex with a woman beside a pool but became impotent; the Prophet told him to seek forgiveness, pray four cycles, and recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r5.anchor: عن يحيى بن جعدة أن رجلا أقبل يريد أن يبشر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمطر فوجد امرأة جالسة على غدير

DURR-FULL:v4p484/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r6.claim: The Prophet compares sins falling through the five prayers after good ablution to dry leaves shaken from a branch.
DURR-FULL:v4p484/r6.anchor: عن سلمان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ غصنا يابسا من شجرة فهزه حتى تحات ورقه

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says the prayers expiate sins committed between them, citing the verse.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جعلت الصلوات كفارات لما بينهن

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says each prayer removes the sins that came before it.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل صلاة تحط ما بين يديها من خطيئة

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r3.speaker: عثمان
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r3.claim: Uthman reports that successive prayers after ablution erase sins from the interval since the previous prayer; he identifies the verse's good deeds as these acts and the enduring good deeds as declarations of remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r3.anchor: عن عثمان قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ ثم قال من توضأ وضوئي هذا

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r4.claim: The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river: they wash away sins as bathing removes dirt.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أرأيتم لو أن بباب أحدكم نهرا

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says God does not erase an evil deed by another evil deed, but erases it by a good deed.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الله لا يمحو السيء بالسيء ولكن السيء بالحسن

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says a fresh good deed is especially effective in pursuing and overtaking an old sin.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لم أر شيئا أحسن طلبا ولا أحسن إدراكا من حسنة حديثة لسيئة قديمة

DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r7.claim: The Prophet tells Mu'adh to follow a bad deed with a good deed so it will erase it.
DURR-FULL:v4p484#2/r7.anchor: عن معاذ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: يا معاذ أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r1.claim: The Prophet describes the daily prayers washing away sins at each prayer time and says nothing is recorded during sleep until waking.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تحترقون فإذا صليتم الصبح غسلتها

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن الجراح
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda urges matching old sins with new good deeds; even sins as vast as heaven and earth can be overcome by a good deed.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح أنه قال: بادروا السيئات القديمات بالحسنات الحديثات

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r3.claim: Hasan likewise urges using new good deeds against old sins, citing the verse as proof.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: استعينوا على السيئات القديمات بالحسنات الحديثات

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r4.claim: The mindful are those who remember God in prosperity and adversity, hardship and ease, health and illness.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين} قال: هم الذين يذكرون الله في السراء والضراء

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the man who kissed the woman remembered the deed afterward, illustrating the verse's “reminder for those who remember.”
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: لما نزع الذي قبل المرأة تذكر فذلك قوله {ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين}

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r1.claim: The two ends of the day are the Maghrib and dawn prayers.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : واقم الصلاة طرفي النهار يقول صلاة المغرب وصلاة الغداه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r2.claim: The ends of the day are morning, noon, and afternoon; Muhammad ibn Ka'b is also reported to hold this view.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن واقم الصلاة طرفي النهار قال الغداء والظهر والعصر وروى عن محمد بن كعب القرظى مثل قول الحسن

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas favored delaying the night prayer and recited “zulfan min al-layl.”
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r3.anchor: سمع عبد الله بن ابى يزيد ابن عباس يستحب تاخير العشاء ويقرا : وزلفا من الليل

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r4.claim: The night intervals refer to the voluntary night prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وزلفا من الليل يقول صلاة القيام

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r5.claim: The two night intervals are Maghrib and Isha; Muhammad ibn Ka'b is also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن وزلفا من الليل قال : هما زلفتان صلاة المغرب وصلاة العشاء - وروى عن محمد بن كعب القرظى مثل قول الحسن

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r6.claim: The two ends of the day mean Fajr and Isha.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهداقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وقال : صلاة الفجر وصلاة العشاء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r7.claim: A man who had kissed a woman asked the Prophet about expiation; the verse was revealed, and the Prophet said it applies to anyone in his community who acts likewise.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r7.anchor: ان رجلا قال : نال من امراة قبله فاتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فساله عن كفارتها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r8.claim: A man said he had done everything with a woman except intercourse, and the verse was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2091#2/r8.anchor: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال اني اصبت منها كل شئ الا الجماع يعني من امراة فانزل الله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says each obligatory prayer expiates sins committed since the preceding prayer; these prayers are the good deeds that erase sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r1.anchor: قال رايت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضا وضوئي هذا ثم قام فصلى صلاة الظهر غفر له

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r2.speaker: عطاء بن دينار
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r2.claim: Tasbih, praise of God, the declaration of divine unity, and the declaration of reliance on God are good deeds and the enduring righteous deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r2.anchor: في قوله : ان الحسنات يذهبن السيئات قال وان من الحسنات قوله : سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا اله الا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r3.claim: Meet old sins with recent good deeds; Hasan finds confirmation in the verse that good deeds erase sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال : استعينوا على السيئات القديمات بالحسنات الحديثات وانكم لن تجدوا شيئا اذهب بسيئة قديمة من حسنة حديثة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r4.claim: A servant is not among those who remember God abundantly until remembering him while standing, sitting, and lying down.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : لا يكون العبد من الذاكرين الله كثيرا حتى يذكر الله قائما وقاعدا ومضطجعا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r5.claim: Those who remember God in prosperity and adversity, hardship and ease, health and affliction are the people reminded by the verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2092/r5.anchor: عن الحسن ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين قال هم الذين يذكرون الله في السراء والضراء والشدة والرخاء والعافية والبلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r1.claim: The statement that good deeds remove sins explains the command to establish prayer; in context, “indeed” emphasizes the claim and signals its causal force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r1.anchor: مسوقة مساق التعليل للأمر بإقامة الصلوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r2.claim: Removing sins can mean good habits make sin easier to avoid, as prayer restrains indecency, or that good deeds erase guilt after a sin; both apply broadly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r2.anchor: وإذهاب السيئات يشمل إذهاب وقوعها بأن يصير انسياق النفس إلى ترك السيئات سهلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r3.claim: Here “sins” means minor sins, limited by verses that exempt minor lapses and promise their erasure when major sins are avoided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r3.anchor: ومحمل السيئات هنا على السيئات الصغائر التي هي من اللمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r4.claim: Bukhari reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who illicitly kissed a woman and asked the Prophet about it; the verse was revealed, and the Prophet said it applies to anyone in his community who does such a deed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r4.anchor: عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أن رجلا أصاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r5.claim: Tirmidhi reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who confessed intimate contact short of intercourse; the Prophet later recited the verse and said it applies to everyone, not only that man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : جاء رجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r6.speaker: الترمذي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Ibn Masud report hasan sahih; he also gives two reports, from Muadh and Abu al-Yusr, and calls those weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p180/r6.anchor: قال الترمذي : هذا حديث حسن صحيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada used the report's “it was revealed to him” wording to argue that this verse, unlike the rest of the surah, is Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r1.anchor: حمل ابن عباس وقتادة على القول بأن هذه الآية مدنية دون بقية هذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r2.claim: If that wording is literal, the verse was inserted here because it fits the preceding command to be upright and the following command to be patient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r2.anchor: هذه الآية ألحقت بهذه السورة في هذا المكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r3.claim: Those who regard the whole surah as Meccan take the verse as a general command to pray, recited by the Prophet to a penitent; “revealed” can mean applying its general rule to his case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r3.anchor: وأما الذين رجحوا أن السورة كلها مكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r4.claim: In another Tirmidhi transmission through Alqama and al-Aswad, Ibn Masud says the Prophet recited the verse, without saying it was newly revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p181/r4.anchor: عن علقمة والأسود عن ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r1.claim: Most early interpreters take the good deeds that erase sins as the five prayers; Uthman invoked this verse while performing ablution, and this is Malik's interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r1.anchor: ذهب جمهور المتأولين من صحابة وتابعين إلى أن الحسنات يراد بها الصلوات الخمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the good deeds are a person's repeated glorification, praise, profession of divine unity, and magnification of God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r3.claim: These are examples of good deeds; the verse's wording is general for good deeds but specific to lesser sins in light of the Prophetic phrase 'if major sins are avoided.'
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r3.anchor: وهذا كله إنما هو على جهة المثال في الحسنات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r4.claim: A report says the verse came after an Ansari man—identified as Abu al-Yusr ibn Amr or as Abbad—met a woman alone and kissed and fondled her without intercourse; after he told Umar and Abu Bakr, he confessed to the Prophet, who recited the verse. Muadh asked if it was only for him; the Prophet said it was for everyone. Another report says the verse predated the incident and was applied to him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r4.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل من الأنصار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said Friday to Friday, the five prayers, and Ramadan to Ramadan expiate what lies between them if major sins are avoided.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r5.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الجمعة إلى الجمعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r6.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r6.claim: Most Sunni scholars make avoiding major sins a condition of the entire promise: without it, the named acts do not expiate lesser sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r6.anchor: فقال جمهورهم: هو شرط في معنى الوعد كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r7.claim: Another group says major sins are the sins the acts do not erase; the condition preserves the hadith's broad wording while the acts still erase lesser sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p212#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معنى قوله إن اجتنبت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya adopts the second interpretation: the hadith about sins falling away with drops of water supports it, provided minor sins are repented of and not persisted in; he calls this the precise view of expert legal theorists. On the first interpretation, the verse applies only to those who avoid major sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r1.anchor: وبهذا أقول وهو الذي يقتضيه حديث خروج الخطايا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r2.claim: ذلك may refer to the prayers as a cause and setting for remembrance, to the claim that good deeds erase sins as encouragement toward good deeds, or to all the preceding commands and prohibitions, as al-Tabari explains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p213/r2.anchor: أي هي سبب ذكر وموضع ذكرى

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r1.claim: طرفي النهار is an adverb governed by أقم; attaching it to الصلاة as the times when prayer occurs is weaker.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r1.anchor: طرفي النهار }: ظرف ل " أقم ". ويضعف أن يكون ظرفا للصلاة

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r2.claim: طرف is not inherently a temporal adverb, but acquires that case after إضافة to a time expression, as in أول النهار and نصف الليل.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r2.anchor: وقرأ العامة " زلفا " بضم الزاي وفتح اللام، وهي جمع " زلفة "

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r3.claim: The common reading زلفا has zay with damma and lam with fatha, a plural of زلفة with a still lam.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن أبي إسحاق بضمها، وفي هذه القراءة ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r4.claim: Their doubled-vowel reading can be a plural of زلفة with vowel harmony, a singular on the pattern of عنق, or a plural of زليف.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r4.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن بإسكان اللام. وفيها وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r5.claim: They read زلفا with a still lam, either as a shortened vocalized form or as an original collective noun.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن أيضا في رواية " وزلفى " بزنة " حبلى "

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r6.speaker: مجاهد وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r6.claim: They also read زلفى as a singular feminine adjective for a near rank or hour; al-Zamakhshari equates it with زلفة.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والزلفى بمعنى الزلفة، كما أن القربى بمعنى القربة "

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r7.claim: زلفا most clearly coordinates with طرفي as a time adverb for the near hours of night; another parse coordinates it with الصلاة as an object.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r7.anchor: وفي انتصاب " زلفا " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه نسق على " طرفي "

SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows coordination with الصلاة, meaning night prayers that draw worshippers near to God.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: بعد أن ذكر القراءات المتقدمة " وهو ما يقرب من آخر النهار ومن الليل

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r1.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r1.claim: Thaʿlab defines زلفة as the first hours of the night.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r1.anchor: والزلفة: أول ساعات الليل، قاله ثعلب.

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش وابن قتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutayba use زلف for the night hours generally, with every hour counting as a zulfa.

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r3.speaker: العجاج
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r3.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse uses زلفا زلفا for successive portions of night.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r3.anchor:
وقال العجاج:
2729 ناج طواه الأين مما وجفا طي الليالي زلفا فزلفا

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r4.claim: The root conveys nearness: أزلفه فازدلف means to bring near and draw close, also used in الشعراء 26:64 and the cited hadith.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r4.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من " الزلفى " وهو القرب، يقال: أزلفه فازدلف، أي: قربه فاقترب.

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r5.claim: Al-Raghib says zulfa can mean rank or favor, can euphemistically denote punishment like بشارة, and gives the related meanings of steps and the name Muzdalifa.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث: " ازدلفوا إلى الله بركعتين "

SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r6.claim: من الليل is an adjective modifying زلفا.
SAMIN-DURR:11:114#2/r6.anchor: وقال الراغب: " والزلفة: المنزلة والحظوة، وقد استعملت الزلفة في معنى العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r1.speaker: علقمة والأسود عن ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r1.claim: A man confessed to the Prophet that he had kissed, embraced, and fondled a woman in a garden without intercourse; after the Prophet fell silent, this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r1.anchor: قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أخذت امرأة في البستان فقبلتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r2.claim: In one report Umar asks whether the verse applies only to the man in the incident; the Prophet answers that it applies to everyone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r2.anchor: فقال عمر أهي له خاصة أم للناس كافة قال لا بل للناس كافة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r3.claim: Another Ibn Masud report says a man told the Prophet he had kissed a woman, and the verse descended; the man asks if it is for him, and the Prophet says it is for whoever acts by it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r3.anchor: أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة فأتى رسول الله فذكر ذلك له فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r4.claim: Muadh reports a man described every unlawful intimacy short of intercourse; the Prophet told him to perform ablution well and pray, then the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r4.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توضأ وضوءا حسنا ثم قم فصل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r5.claim: Abu Salih identifies the man as Amr ibn Ghaziya al-Ansari, a date seller who lured a customer by claiming better dates were at home.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r5.anchor: هو عمرو بن غزية الأنصاري وفيه نزلت هذه الآية كان يبيع التمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r6.claim: Muqatil identifies the man as Abu Miqbal Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل هو أبو مقبل عامر بن قيس الأنصاري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r7.speaker: أحمد بن علي بن ثابت الخطيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r7.claim: Al-Khatib identifies the man as Abu al-Yusr Ka'b ibn Amr al-Ansari.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r7.anchor: وذكر أحمد بن علي بن ثابت الخطيب الحافظ أنه أبو اليسر كعب بن عمرو الأنصاري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r8.claim: The source gives three possible questioners asking whether the ruling was special: Abu al-Yusr, Muadh ibn Jabal, or Umar ibn al-Khattab.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r8.anchor: ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه أبو اليسر صاحب القصة والثاني معاذ بن جبل والثالث عمر بن الخطاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r9.claim: “Establish prayer” means perform its bowing and prostration completely.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r9.anchor: فأما التفسير فقوله ( وأقم الصلاة ) أي أتم ركوعها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r10.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r10.claim: The first end of the day is the dawn prayer according to the majority; Ibn Jarir instead reports the noon prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p165#3/r10.anchor: في الطرف الأول قولان أحدهما أنه صلاة الفجر قاله الجمهور والثاني أنه الظهر حكاه ابن جرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd identify the second end of the day with the sunset prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه صلاة المغرب قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r2.speaker: قتادة والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the second end with the afternoon prayer; al-Hasan is reported to hold either this or the sunset view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r2.anchor: الثاني العصر قاله قتادة وعن الحسن كالقولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r3.speaker: مجاهد والقرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Qurazi identify the second end of the day with both noon and afternoon prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r3.anchor: والثالث الظهر والعصر قاله مجاهد والقرظي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak is reported to accept all three interpretations of the second end of the day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far and Shayba read zulafan with a ḍamma on the lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة و زلفا بضم اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والعجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda explains zulaf as hours or stages, singular zulfa; al-Ajjaj's poem uses it for successive nighttime intervals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r6.anchor: الزلف الساعات واحدها زلفة أي ساعة ومنزلة وقربة ومنه سميت المزدلفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba connects the term with drawing near: azlafani means brought me close, and mazalif are stages or steps.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r7.anchor: ومنه يقال أزلفني كذا عندك أي أدناني والمزالف المنازل والدرج وكذلك الزلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r8.claim: One interpretation identifies the nighttime intervals as the late evening prayer, reported from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Mujahid and adopted by Ibn Zayd.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r8.anchor: أحدهما أنها صلاة العتمة رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وعوف عن الحسن وابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد وبه قال ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة ومقاتل والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r9.claim: The other interpretation identifies them as sunset and night prayers; reports and named authorities support this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p167/r9.anchor: والثاني أنها صلاة المغرب والعشاء روي عن ابن عباس أيضا ورواه يونس عن الحسن ومنصور عن مجاهد وبه قال قتادة ومقاتل والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن المسيب ومسروق ومجاهد والقرظي والضحاك ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r1.claim: These authorities identify the good deeds that erase sins as the five daily prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنها الصلوات الخمس قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن المسيب ومسروق ومجاهد والقرظي والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r2.speaker: منصور عن مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r2.claim: Mansur transmits from Mujahid that the good deeds are saying “Glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر رواه منصور عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r3.claim: The author prefers the five-prayer interpretation because most authorities hold it and a connected Prophetic report supports it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r3.anchor: والأول أصح لأن الجمهور عليه وفيه حديث مسند عن رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r4.speaker: عثمان عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r4.claim: Uthman reports that ablution followed by each prayer expiates sins committed since the preceding prayer; these prayers are the good deeds that erase sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r4.anchor: من توضأ وضوئي هذا ثم صلى الظهر غفر له ما كان بينها وبين صلاة الصبح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r5.claim: The commentators identify the sins erased here as minor sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r5.anchor: فأما السيئات المذكورة هاهنا فقال المفسرون هي الصغائر من الذنوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r6.speaker: معاذ بن جبل عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r6.claim: Muadh reports the Prophet's advice to fear God, follow a bad deed with a good one to erase it, and treat people well.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p168/r6.anchor: أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها قلت زدني قال خالق الناس بخلق حسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r1.claim: “That” may refer to the Qur'an, the establishment of prayer, or all preceding counsel: steadfastness, avoiding transgression and unjust rulers, and prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r1.anchor: في المشار إليه ب ذلك ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r2.claim: The word “reminder” is interpreted either as repentance or as admonition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p169/r2.anchor: وفي المراد بالذكرى قولان أحدهما أنه بمعنى التوبة والثاني بمعنى العظة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Hasan, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identify the two ends of day as morning and sunset prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: يعني الصبح والمغرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p354#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
