TABRISI:11:114#2/r3.claim: One interpretation is that persistence in good deeds leads a person to abandon evil deeds, as though the good deeds remove them.
TABRISI:11:114#2/r3.anchor: الدوام على فعل الحسنات يدعو إلى ترك السيئات فكأنها يذهبن بها

TABRISI:11:114#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:114#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:114#2/r4.claim: A second interpretation identifies the good deeds as repentance, which removes sins by cancelling their punishment; the author says there is no disagreement that repentance cancels punishment.
TABRISI:11:114#2/r4.anchor: المراد بالحسنات التوبة فإنها تذهب السيئات بأن تسقط عقابها

TABRISI:11:114#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:114#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:114#2/r5.claim: The reminder is an admonition for whoever reflects on the teaching that good deeds remove evil deeds.
TABRISI:11:114#2/r5.anchor: فيه تذكار وموعظة لمن تذكر به وفكر فيه

THALABI:v5p193/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v5p193/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the good deeds that erase sins with the five daily prayers.
THALABI:v5p193/r1.anchor: إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات يعني: إن الصلوات الخمس يذهبن الخطيئات

THALABI:v5p193/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p193/r2.claim: Mujahid says the good deeds are saying glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and God’s greatness.
THALABI:v5p193/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي قول العبد: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

THALABI:v5p193/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p193/r3.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu al-Yusr, a date seller who embraced and kissed a woman he had lured home, stopped when she reminded him of God, then confessed to the Prophet.
THALABI:v5p193/r3.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي اليسر عمرو بن غزية الأنصاري وكان يبيع التمر

THALABI:v5p193/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r4.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p193/r4.claim: After Gabriel brought the verse following the afternoon prayer, the Prophet told Abu al-Yusr that the prayer expiated his act; when Umar asked if this applied only to him, the Prophet said it applied to everyone.
THALABI:v5p193/r4.anchor: قال: «أشهدت معنا هذه الصلاة؟» قال: نعم، قال: «اذهب فإنها كفارة لما عملت»

THALABI:v5p193/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p193/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p193/r5.claim: The phrase that follows may point back to what was just mentioned, or alternatively to the Quran as a reminder for those who remember.
THALABI:v5p193/r5.anchor: ذلك الذي ذكرناه، وقيل: هو إشارة إلى القرآن ذكرى عظة للذاكرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r1.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r1.claim: The verse followed a man's question about sexual contact short of intercourse; the Prophet told him to perform ablution and pray, then said the ruling applies to everyone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r1.anchor: قال عامة المفسرين (¬5): نزلت في رجل أتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: ما تقول في رجل أصاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, the two ends of the day are dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) في رواية عطاء في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} يريد الصبح والظهر والعصر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid, in the report of Manṣūr, identifies the prayers at the two ends as dawn, noon, and afternoon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد (¬4) في رواية منصور # والقرظي (¬1)، واختيار الفراء (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj identifies the day-end prayers as dawn, noon, and afternoon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: وصلاة طرفي النهار: الغداة والظهر والعصر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r5.claim: Muqātil adds the sunset prayer, assigning dawn and noon to one end and afternoon and sunset to the other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r5.anchor: وزاد مقاتل (¬4): المغرب، وقال: صلاة الفجر والظهر طرف وصلاة العصر والمغرب طرف،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r6.claim: The correct view is al-Zajjāj's: dawn is one end, noon and afternoon the other, while sunset belongs to the night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r6.anchor: والصحيح ما ذكره الزجاج، وذلك أن أحد طرفي النهار صلاة الصبح والآخر فيه صلاتا (¬5) العشاء،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identifies the ends as dawn and sunset; al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r7.anchor: ويروى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد (¬6) أنهما قالا: صلاة طرفي النهار الفجر والمغرب،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r8.claim: The wording's apparent sense supports dawn and sunset; noon and afternoon are omitted because their place in daytime prayer is obvious and they are specified in 17:78.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p578#2/r8.anchor: وظاهر الكلام يدل على هذا، وحذف ذكر الظهر والعصر لظهور أمرهما في صلاة النهار؛ لأنهما أفردا بالذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r1.claim: The five daily prayers expiate the sins between them, provided major sins are avoided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون (¬5): يريد [إن الصلوات الخمس] (¬6) تكفر ما بينها من الذنوب إذا اجتنبت الكبائر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r2.claim: Through Layth, Mujāhid says the good deeds are the devotional phrases “Glory be to God,” praise, the testimony of faith, and takbīr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r2.anchor: وروى ليث عن مجاهد (¬7) قال: هي قول العبد: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r3.claim: ذلك is used in the sense of هذا: “this is an admonition.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: هذا موعظة ف (ذلك) عنده بمعنى (هذا)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes ذلك ذكرى to mean that the Quran is an admonition for whoever remembers it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r4.anchor: وقال غيره (¬1): {ذلك ذكرى} يعني القرآن عظة لمن ذكره،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r5.claim: ذكرى is a verbal noun ending in feminine alif, patterned like العدوى and الدعوى, or like شورى; the text also discusses its plural and the variant ذِكر.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r5.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: الذكرى مصدر جاء بألف التأنيث، كما جاء على فعلى نحو العدوى والدعوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r6.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r6.claim: Sībawayh records the form الذكر with dāl; Ibn Muqbil's line uses that form, which resembles words such as تقوى and تقية.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p582/r6.anchor: وقالوا في الجمع (للذكر) فجعلوه بمنزلة (سدرة وسدر)، كما جعلوا (العلى) مثل (الظلم)،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r1.claim: “The two ends of day” are the morning and sunset prayers, while the early portions of night mean the ʿishāʾ prayer near nightfall.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r1.anchor: طرفي النهار } بالصبح والمغرب { وزلفا من الليل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r2.claim: Another interpretation counts the ends of day as dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers, with sunset and night prayers among the early night prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r2.anchor: وقيل: صلاة طرفي النهار: الفجر والظهر والعصر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r3.claim: The five prayers expiate sins committed between them when major sins are avoided.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r3.anchor: إن الصلوات الخمس تكفر ما بينها من الذنوب إذا اجتنبت الكبائر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r4.claim: This is an admonition for people who remember and take heed.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the two ends of the day run from the dawn prayer to the afternoon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r5.anchor: وحدثني قرة بن خالد عن الحسن في قوله: {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} [هود: 114] قال: ما بين صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the ends of the day as dawn and afternoon prayers, and the near parts of night as Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r1.anchor: طرفا النهار: صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر.

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r1.claim: “Zulaf” is the plural of “zulfa,” whose Arabic broken plural denotes at least three; with two parts of the day, this indicates five prayers, including three during the night’s approaches to day.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r1.anchor: “Zülef” “zülfe”nin cem‘i ve Arabîde cem‘in ekalli üç olduğu için bununla ikisi gündüz tarafında, üçü de geceden olmak üzere tam beş vakit namaz emredilmiş olduğu zâhirdir

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r2.claim: On the reading that dawn counts among night prayers, the two day parts are noon and afternoon, while the three night-adjacent times are sunset, evening, and dawn; the author links this arrangement to 17:78.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r2.anchor: “tarafeyi’n-nehâr”dan murad öğle ve ikindi, “zülefen mine’lleyl” de akşam, yatsı, sabah

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r3.claim: Noon and afternoon can be called the day’s two parts because dawn is its root, sunrise to noon its body, and noon through afternoon its prominent later divisions; another verse also speaks of the day’s parts.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r3.anchor: Sabah gündüzün kökü, Güneş’in tulû‘undan zevâline kadar da gövdesi, zevalden sonra öğle ve ikindi de gurûbuna kadar tehavvülâtının bariz hadleri

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r4.claim: Most scholars instead take the phrase as dawn and afternoon, or morning and sunset, supported by the wording “before sunrise and before sunset”; this leaves noon, which other verses state explicitly, unmentioned here.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r4.anchor: sabah ve ikindi olması lâzım geleceğine kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and many others read one day part as before noon and the other as after it, yielding dawn, noon, and afternoon within the two parts and incorporating dawn as one of the day’s parts.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r5.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf gibi birçokları da bir tarafı zevalden evveli, bir tarafı da zevalden sonrası yani gudüv ve aşiy mânasına hamletmişlerdir

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r6.claim: On that interpretation, the three night parts imply six obligatory prayers: the Prophet’s additional obligatory tahajjud and the community’s witr; other plural wording also suggests at least six.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r6.anchor: farz namazların beş değil altı olması iktizâ eder

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r7.claim: Five prayers are certain through several proofs, while a sixth is only probable; therefore witr is a practical obligation (wājib), not an obligation of belief.

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r8.claim: Elmalılı prefers taking the two day parts as two of the customary three divisions, noon and afternoon, because the opposing “night approaches” clarify the phrase; with sunset, evening, and dawn, this gives the five daily prayers.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r8.anchor: gündüzün iki ucu veya ortasının iki yanı demek olmayıp örfte başlıca üç sayılan etrâf-ı nehârdan ikisi demek olması bizce

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r9.claim: These five prayers are established and performed with congregation; the call announcing the prayer is sunnah and congregational prayer is wājib.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r9.anchor: tam beş vakit namazdır ki ikāmet ve cemaatle kılınır. İkāmet sünnet, cemaat vâcibdir

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r10.claim: Each prayer is a good deed that continually erases prior minor sins; the five daily prayers expiate sins between them when major sins are avoided, as a hadith states.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r10.anchor: beş vakit namaz arada vâki‘olan küçük günahlara keffaret olur

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r11.claim: A hadith says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r11.anchor: namaz, namaza kadar aralarındakine keffarettir, kebâirden ictinab ettikçe

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r12.claim: Because prayer restrains indecency and evil, regular prayer cultivates aversion to sins, avoidance of major sins, and remorse and repentance for any major sin already committed.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r12.anchor: namaza devam edildikçe ale’l-umûm seyyiâta karşı hiss-i nefret uyanır

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r13.claim: “That” may refer to the prayer or to the address from the command to be steadfast through this passage; either way, it is a reminder for people who heed.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r13.anchor: O namaz yahut فَٱسْتَقِمْ emrinden buraya kadar olan hitâbe

ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.claim: The positive commands are addressed grammatically to the Prophet but apply to everyone, while prohibitions address the community; this rhetorical shift implies that transgression and inclination to oppressors are inconceivable for the Prophet but possible among his community.
ELMALILI:11:114-115/r14.anchor: zâhiren müfred olarak Resûlullah’a hitab edilmiş, hâlbuki mâna itibariyle emir, umûma yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r1.claim: Day runs from dawn to sunset and night from sunset to dawn; the day’s two edges are dawn and sunset. The prayer at the second edge is variously identified as noon and afternoon before sunset, or sunset and night prayers after it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r1.anchor: Gündüzün iki tarafından maksat, geceyle birleşen iki tarafı, yani başı ve sonu olup tan yerinin ağardığı ve güneşin battığı zamanlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r2.claim: Zulef, plural of zulfa, means the night’s early hours near day and refers here to the night prayer; because the verse gives no form or exact times, it stresses prayer at the indicated periods without detailing them, as Shawkani notes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r2.anchor: “Gündüze yakın saatler” diye tercüme ettiğimiz zülef kelimesi ise zülfenin çoğulu olup gecenin gündüze yakın olan ilk saatlerini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r3.speaker: some interpreters
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r3.claim: Some hold that this verse sets the times for all obligatory prayers; the mutawatir Sunna supplies their specific times and manner.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r3.anchor: Bu âyetin bütün farz namazların vakitlerini belirlediği kanaatinde olanlar da vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r4.claim: The verse calls for worship and abundant good deeds to remove or forgive evils, especially prayer, and its closing words address those who turn toward Qur’anic guidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:114/r4.anchor: Âyet, kötülüklerin ortadan kalkması veya bağışlanması için ibadetlerle iyiliklerin çokça yapılmasının gereğine işaret etmektedir

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p115#4/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p115#4/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p115#4/r15.claim: The statement إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات was revealed concerning Nabḥān al-Tammār.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p115#4/r15.anchor: وقوله: إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات نزلت في نبهان التمار

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r9.claim: The command is to establish the prescribed prayer at its known times; prayer is the believer's ascent, as reports attest its lofty rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r9.anchor: أمر بإقامة الصلاة المفروضة على ما علمت وقد ذكروا أن الصلاة معراج المؤمن وفي الأخبار ما يدل على علو شأنها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r10.speaker: الواسطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r10.claim: Al-Wasiti says the lights of acts of obedience remove the darkness of acts of disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r10.anchor: قال الواسطي : أنوار الطاعات تذهب بظلم المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r11.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r11.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh says God covers a believer's sin, then forgives it, then replaces it with good deeds, citing 25:70.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r11.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : إن الله سبحانه لم يرض للمؤمن بالذنب حتى ستر ولم يرض بالستر حتى غفر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r12.claim: Prayer at the stated times and good deeds erasing wrongs remind those who remember God of presence, purity, gatheredness, intimacy, and spiritual taste.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r12.anchor: ذكرى للذاكرين تذكير لمن يذكر حاله عند الحضور مع الله تعالى في الصفاء والجمعية والأنس والذوق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r5.claim: A nominal clause such as إن تأتني أنا كريم cannot normally answer a conditional, since it begins independently rather than attaching to what precedes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r5.anchor: أن يضطر شاعر من قبل أن أنا كريم يكون كلاما مبتدأ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r6.claim: Poets may use an independent nominal answer under necessity; Sībawayh cites lines by Hassan ibn Thabit and al-Asadi as examples.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r7.claim: إن تأتني لأفعلن is normally unsuitable because the oath lām clause begins independently; with لئن, the oath lām may be understood or stated.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r9.claim: A past-tense condition can follow its answer, as in Zuhayr's line; reversing a present-tense إن clause is normally disfavored because إن governs the verb.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r10.claim: Poetry can postpone a present-tense conditional clause after its answer, as in Jarir's line and the saying about the man who meets bribes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/r10.anchor: يا أقرع بن حابس يا أقرع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r1.claim: Zulfa means drawing nearer gradually; in the verse it broadly conveys nearness and drawing close.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r1.anchor: الزلفة بمعنى تقرّب إليه، تزلّف إليه أي تقرّب إليه شيئاً فشيئاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r2.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r2.claim: Many commentators understand the near portions of night as the prayers closest to daytime, namely Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r2.anchor: الزُلَف من الليل أي ما هو أقرب إلى النهار وهما صلاتي المغرب والعشاء. هذا يراه كثير من المفسرين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r3.claim: Some interpret it as drawing near to God through night prayer, without restricting it to Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r3.anchor: بعضهم يرى أن معناه تقرّب إلى الله بصلاة الليل وليس بالضرورة صلاة المغرب والعشاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p987/r4.claim: He concludes that zulfa carries the general sense of drawing near.

NASHR:v1p288/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p288/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p288/r1.claim: In the large-idghām inventory, assimilation before jīm has seventeen cases, including الصالحات جناح; before dhāl there are nine, including السيئات ذلك and الآخرة ذلك.
NASHR:v1p288/r1.anchor: الصالحات جناح وجملته سبعة عشر حرفا

NASHR:v1p288/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p288/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p288/r9.claim: Three ṭāʾ environments are listed; in ولتأت طائفة, readers who assimilate other jussives assimilate, while those who articulate them clearly do so here, though homorganicity and the strong ṭāʾ favor assimilation. Al-Dānī and most accept both.
NASHR:v1p288/r9.anchor: إلا أن الإدغام قوي هنا من أجل التجانس وقوة الكسر والطاء

NASHR:v1p288/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p288/r11.speaker: ابن حبش
NASHR:v1p288/r11.claim: Ibn Ḥabash alone reports that al-Sūsī clearly articulates الصلاة طرفي النهار because the vowel is light and the preceding consonant is still; other performance authorities assimilate for homorganicity and the strength of ṭāʾ.
NASHR:v1p288/r11.anchor: وانفرد ابن حبش عن السوسي بإظهار الصلاة طرفي النهار

NASHR:v2p291/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p291/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p291/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ṭalḥa, Shayba, ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr, and named transmitters from Abū ʿAmr read زلفا with ḍamma on lām; the others read it with fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p291/r5.anchor: وزلفا من فقرأ أبو جعفر بضم اللام

NASHR:v2p291/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p291/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p291/r6.claim: Both vowels are attested dialects in the plural of زلفة, meaning a portion of the early night, as in ظُلَم/ظلمة and يُسْر/يُسْرة.
NASHR:v2p291/r6.anchor: ظلم في ظلمة ويسر في يسرة

NASHR:v1p206/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p206/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet recited in taḥqīq through the transmission given by the author; al-Dānī calls it rare and known only by this route, but with a sound chain.
NASHR:v1p206/r1.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني هذا الحديث غريب لا أعلمه يحفظ

NASHR:v1p206/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p206/r2.claim: Al-Dānī calls the report a major basis for the duty to practice taḥqīq and learn precision and tajwīd, citing its connected chain and reliable transmitters.
NASHR:v1p206/r2.anchor: هذا الخبر الوارد بتوقيف قراءة التحقيق من الأخبار الغريبة والسنن العزيزة

NASHR:v1p206/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p206/r3.claim: Ḥadr derives from “descending quickly” and means a rapid, compressed recitation using reported shortening, stilling, ikhtilās, substitution, large assimilation, and eased hamza while preserving connection, inflection, and clear letter production; it opposes taḥqīq.
NASHR:v1p206/r3.anchor: فهو عندهم عبارة عن إدراج القراءة وسرعتها وتخفيفها بالقصر والتسكين والاختلاس

NASHR:v1p206/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p206/r4.claim: Ḥadr can increase recitation's reward, but must not truncate madd, erase ghunna, overly shorten vowels, invalidate recitation, or leave the bounds of tartīl.
NASHR:v1p206/r4.anchor: فالحدر يكون لتكثير الحسنات في القراءة، وحوز فضيلة التلاوة

NASHR:v1p206/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NASHR:v1p206/r5.claim: A man told Ibn Masʿūd he had recited the Mufaṣṣal in one rakʿa; Ibn Masʿūd rebuked this as reciting like poetry, in a report cited from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.
NASHR:v1p206/r5.anchor: ففي صحيح البخاري أن رجلا جاء إلى ابن مسعود

NASHR:v1p206/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p206/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p206/r6.claim: Ḥadr is associated with Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, and readers who shorten the separated madd, including Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, Qālūn, al-Aṣbahānī from Warsh, al-Walī from Ḥafṣ, and most Iraqi transmitters from al-Ḥulwānī from Hishām.
NASHR:v1p206/r6.anchor: مذهب ابن كثير وأبي جعفر وسائر من قصر المنفصل

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī treats applying “lafẓ” to sounds and letters as metaphorical: breath is expelled from the chest; it causes the words and makes their production resemble casting them outward.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: إطلاق اللفظ على هذه الأصوات والحروف على سبيل المجاز وذلك لأنها إنما تحدث عند إخراج النفس من داخل الصدر إلى الخارج

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: All six permutations of the root ع ب ر signify crossing or transition.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: وهي في تقاليبها الستة تفيد العبور والانتقال

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: Under ع ب ر, “expression” involves moving from letter to letter and transferring meaning from the speaker’s mind to the listener.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: لا يمكنه أن يتكلم بها إلا إذا انتقل من حرف إلى حرف آخر

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: Under ع ب ر, العبرة is a tear moving from inside the eye outward, while العبر denotes crossing from the witnessed to the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: ومنه العبرة لأن تلك الدمعة تنتقل من داخل العين إلى الخارج ومنه العبر لأن الإنسان ينتقل فيها من الشاهد إلى الغائب

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: The word معبر denotes a crossing because a person passes by it from one side of the sea to the other.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: ومنه المعبر لأن الإنسان ينتقل بواسطته من أحد طرفي البحر إلى الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r6.claim: The word التعبير denotes moving from what one sees in a dream to hidden meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r6.anchor: ومنه التعبير لأنه ينتقل مما يراه في النوم إلى المعاني الغائبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r7.claim: Under ع ر ب, Arabs are so named for their frequent movements on the winter and summer journeys.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r7.anchor: الثاني ع ر ب ومنه تسمية العرب بالعرب لكثرة انتقالاتهم بسبب رحلة الشتاء والصيف

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r8.claim: Under ع ر ب, iʿrāb moves an utterance from obscurity before inflection to knowledge and clarity after inflection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r8.anchor: فلان أعرب في كلامه لأن اللفظ قبل الإعراب يكون مجهولا فإذا دخله الإعراب انتقل إلى المعرفة والبيان

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r9.claim: Under ب ر ع, برع means becoming complete and increasing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r9.anchor: الثالث ب ر ع ومنه فلان برع في كذا إذا تكامل وتزايد

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r10.claim: Under ب ع ر, البعر is linked to movement from the inside to the outside.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r10.anchor: الرابع ب ع ر ومنه البعر لكونه منتقلا من الداخل إلى الخارج

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r11.claim: Under ر ع ب, fear is called رعب because a person shifts from one state to another when it occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r11.anchor: الخامس ر ع ب ومنه يقال للخوف رعب لأن الإنسان ينتقل عند حدوثه من حال إلى حال أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r12.claim: Under ر ب ع, الربع is a place people move from and to.
RAZI-FULL:v1p25/r12.anchor: والسادس ر ب ع ومنه الربع لأن الناس ينتقلون منها وإليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: Short vowels are parts of the long-vowel letters: those letters admit increase and decrease, their lower limit is the short vowels, and lengthening a short vowel yields a long vowel; usage also favors substituting a part for its whole.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: الحركات أبعاض من حروف المد واللين ويدل عليه وجوه الأول

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: Some hold that beginning with a vowelless consonant is impossible because a vowel sound follows articulation of the consonant; others permit it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: الابتداء بالحرف الساكن محال عند قوم وجائز عند آخرين

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: The ḍamma is the heaviest vowel, requiring both lips and two muscles; kasra needs one muscle, while fatḥa requires only a slight effort, as anatomy and experience show.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: أثقل الحركات الضمة لأنها لا تتم إلا بضم الشفتين ولا يتم ذلك إلا بعمل العضلتين الصلبتين

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: Vowel coloring varies by regional constitution: Azerbaijanis tend to color their words with ḍamma, while many regions tend toward kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: فإن أهل أذربيجان يغلب على جميع ألفاظهم إشمام الضمة وكثير من البلاد يغلب على لغاتهم إشمام الكسرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r5.claim: When the three vowels and sukūn are inflectional, they are called nominative, accusative, genitive or lowered, and jussive; when structural, they are called fatḥ, ḍamm, kasr, and pause.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r5.anchor: الحركات الثلاثة مع السكون إن كانت إعرابية سميت بالرفع والنصب والجر أو الخفض والجزم

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r6.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r6.claim: Quṭrub holds that structural vowels are like inflectional vowels.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r6.anchor: ذهب قطرب إلى أن الحركات البنائية مثل الإعرابية

RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī calls the dispute verbal: the vowels are perceptually identical in essence, but they are not equally warranted by differing grammatical governors.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48/r7.anchor: وهذا الخلاف لفظي فإن المراد من التماثل إن كان هو التماثل في الماهية فالحس يشهد بأن الأمر كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r1.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r1.claim: Ahl al-Sunna argue that if human capacity is directed to only one alternative, compulsion follows; if it can support both, preference needs a determinant, whose agent either repeats the dilemma or makes action necessary or impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r1.anchor: قال أهل السنة والجماعة : أما الإشكالات التي ألزمتموها علينا ؛ فهي بأسرها واردة عليكم من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r2.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r2.claim: They reject uncaused preference: it would undermine inference from a possible outcome’s preference to a determinant and leave the act as chance, not the servant’s doing, returning to sheer compulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r2.anchor: أن على هذا التقدير يكون ذلك الرجحان واقعا على سبيل الاتفاق ولا يكون صادرا عن العبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r3.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r3.claim: They argue that an act contrary to God’s knowledge would turn divine knowledge into ignorance; the same objection raised against predestination therefore applies to foreknowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r3.anchor: قال أهل السنة والجماعة : أما الإشكالات التي ألزمتموها علينا ؛ فهي بأسرها واردة عليكم من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r4.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r4.claim: They argue that seeking refuge from Satan refutes predestination: if it asks God to prevent temptation by warning, that prevention has already occurred; if by coercion, it conflicts with the jinn’s accountability.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r4.anchor: ثم قال أهل السنة والجماعة : قوله : ^ { أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم } ^ يبطل القول بالقدر من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites reply that seeking refuge asks for divine graces that encourage the accountable person to do good and avoid evil; some graces are fitting only after the supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r5.anchor: أجابت المعتزلة عنه فقالوا : المطلوب بالاستعاذة فعل الألطاف التي تدعو المكلف إلى فعل الحسن وترك القبيح

RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r6.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r6.claim: Ahl al-Sunna answer that if such graces tip the balance toward action, the action becomes necessary and undercuts Muʿtazilite freedom; if they do not, they have no effect and are futile.
RAZI-FULL:v1p65/r6.anchor: أجاب أهل السنة عن هذا السؤال : بأن فعل تلك الألطاف إما أن يكون له أثر في ترجيح جانب الفعل على جانب الترك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi says he heard Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm and transmitted from him; Abu Bakr al-Khwarizmi appointed him to teach his lesson during his absence.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi notes that he wrote major works and critical supplements addressing leading scholars of language and grammar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r2.anchor: وله المصنفات الكبار، والاستدراكات على الفحول من علماء اللغة والنحو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r3.claim: He studied intensively with al-Thaʿlabi for years, visiting daily to hear, read, annotate, memorize, research and discuss while working through poetry collections and language books.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r3.anchor: وكنت قد لازمته سنين، أدخل عليه عند طلوع الشمس، وأخرج لغروبها، أسمع، وأقرأ، وأعلق، وأحفظ، وأبحث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r4.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi urged him to devote himself to Quran commentary; al-Wahidi replied that literary study prepared him for tafsir and continued visiting until death separated them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r4.anchor: إنك لم تبق ديوانا من الشعر إلا قضيت حقه، أما آن لك أن تتفرغ لتفسير كتاب الله العزيز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r5.claim: As a young man he studied under Abu al-Hasan al-Darir, whom he describes as outstanding in subtle grammar and the intricacies of Arabic, and devoted to training him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r5.anchor: وكان من أبرع أهل زمانه في لطائف النحو وغوامضه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r6.claim: Under al-Darir, al-Wahidi studied grammar, morphology and semantics, compiled nearly one hundred fascicles on difficult issues, heard works on grammar, metrics and linguistic causes, and received his book on Ibn Mihran's qiraat justifications.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r6.anchor: وقرأت عليه جوامع النحو والتصريف والمعاني، وعلقت عنه قريبا من مائة جزء في المسائل المشكلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r7.claim: He studied with Abu al-Hasan Imran al-Maghribi al-Maliki, whom he calls unmatched in i'rab, and says he absorbed the finest of his knowledge during his stay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p418/r7.anchor: ثم ورد علينا الشيخ الإمام أبو الحسن عمران بن موسى المغربي المالكي

BURHAN:v1p29/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.claim: An ayah may descend twice to magnify its importance and recall it when a new cause arises; the Fatiha is said to have descended once in Mecca and once in Medina, and this resolves the report about the Makkan Hūd verse.
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.anchor: وقد ينزل الشىء مرتين تعظيما لشأنه وتذكيرا به عند حدوث سببه خوف نسيانه وهذا كما قيل فى الفاتحة نزلت مرتين

BURHAN:v1p29/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURHAN:v1p29/r2.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥs, a man who had kissed a woman told the Prophet, and this verse was revealed; the Prophet said it applies to the whole community. Al-Tirmidhi or another source identifies the man as Abū al-Yusr.
BURHAN:v1p29/r2.anchor: ثبت فى الصحيحين عن أبى عثمان النهدى عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة فأتى النبى

BURHAN:v1p29/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.claim: A new question or incident can prompt the Prophet to receive an ayah that had already descended; its repetition reminds people of the text and shows that it encompasses the new event's ruling.
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.anchor: والحكمة فى هذا كله أنه قد يحدث سبب من سؤال أو حادثة تقتضى نزول آية وقد نزل قبل ذلك ما يتضمنها

BURHAN:v1p196/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p196/r2.claim: The Hūd verse is reported as revealed concerning Abū Miqbal al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar ibn Qays and a woman who bought dates from him, whom he tried to seduce.

ITQAN:v1p48/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p48/r1.claim: Three verses are excepted from the classification of Hūd as Meccan, including the command to pray at the two ends of the day.
ITQAN:v1p48/r1.anchor: هود استثني منها ثلاث آيات ﴿ فلعلك تارك ﴾ ﴿ أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ﴾ ﴿ وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار ﴾

ITQAN:v1p48/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p48/r2.claim: The author supports the Medinan classification of the third exception with sound reports through several routes, saying it concerned Abū al-Yusr.
ITQAN:v1p48/r2.anchor: قلت دليل الثالثة ما صح من عدة طرق أنها نزلت بالمدينة في حق أبي اليسر

ITQAN:v1p104/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p104/r5.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p104/r5.claim: Al-Zarkashī says revelation may recur to magnify a verse, renew its reminder when its occasion arises, and prevent its being forgotten; he cites 11:114.
ITQAN:v1p104/r5.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان قد ينزل الشيء مرتين تعظيما لشأنه وتذكيرا عند حدوث سببه خوف نسيانه ثم ذكر منه آية الروح وقوله

ITQAN:v1p104/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.claim: Al-Zarkashī resolves the apparent clash between the Meccan status of al-Isrāʾ and Hūd and Medinan reports about their occasions by saying the verses descended twice.
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.anchor: قال فإن سورة الإسراء وهود مكيتان وسبب نزولهما يدل على أنهما نزلتا بالمدينة ولهذا أشكل ذلك على بعضهم

ITQAN:v1p251/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p251/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p251/r1.claim: Large assimilation covers sixteen letters, under mnemonic رض سنشد حجتك بذل قثم; the first consonant must not be geminated, tanwīn, or a pronoun tāʾ.
ITQAN:v1p251/r1.anchor: وأما المدغم من المتجانسين والمتقاربين فهو ستة عشر حرفا يجمعها رض سنشد حجتك بذل قثم وشرطه ألا يكون الأول مشددا

ITQAN:v1p251/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p251/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p251/r3.claim: Tāʾ assimilates into ten following letters, including ṭāʾ in the phrase about prayer at the two ends of the day.

ITQAN:v1p251/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p251/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p251/r5.claim: Thāʾ assimilates into five letters; jīm into shīn and tāʾ; and ḥāʾ into ʿayn only in زحزح عن النار.
ITQAN:v1p251/r5.anchor: والثاء في خمسة أحرف التاء ﴿ حيث تؤمرون ﴾ والذال ﴿ والحرث ذلك ﴾ والسين ﴿ وورث سليمان ﴾

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r1.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥiṣār requires an explicit transmission from the Prophet or a Companion stating that one verse abrogated another to establish abrogation.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن الحصار إنما يرجع في النسخ إلى نقل صريح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو عن صحابي يقول آية كذا نسخت كذا

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r2.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Ḥiṣār also allows abrogation to be inferred from certain chronology when a definite contradiction requires identifying which ruling came first.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r2.anchor: قال وقد يحكم به عند وجود التعارض المقطوع به من علم التاريخ ليعرف المتقدم والمتأخر

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r3.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Ḥiṣār rejects claims based only on lay commentators or independent juristic reasoning without reliable transmission and clear contradiction; abrogation depends on transmission and chronology, not opinion.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r3.anchor: قال ولا يعتمد في النسخ قول عوام المفسرين بل ولا اجتهاد المجتهدين من غير نقل صحيح ولا معارضة بينة

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r4.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Ḥiṣār rejects both extremes: refusing sound solitary reports altogether and accepting a commentator's or jurist's claim without evidence.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r4.anchor: قال والناس في هذا بين طرفي نقيض فمن قائل لا يقبل في النسخ أخبار الآحاد العدول ومن متساهل يكتفي فيه بقول مفسر أو مجتهد والصواب خلاف قولهما

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الفنون
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r5.claim: For abrogation of recitation while retaining the ruling, Ṣāḥib al-Funūn says the wisdom is to show the community's readiness to obey on probable evidence, like Abraham's response to his dream.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r5.anchor: وأجاب صاحب الفنون بأن ذلك ليظهر به مقدار طاعة هذه الأمة في المسارعة إلى بذل النفوس بطريق الظن

ITQAN:v3p65#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar warns against claiming to possess the whole Qur'an because much of it has gone, advising people to say they have what remains apparent.
ITQAN:v3p65#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال لا يقولن أحدكم قد أخذت القرآن كله وما يدريه ما كله قد ذهب منه قرآن كثير

ITQAN:v3p116/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p116/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p116/r1.claim: The fragment compares trying to keep water in a cupped hand, which leaves nothing, to the elusive nature of worldly life.
ITQAN:v3p116/r1.anchor: أن الماء إذا طبقت عليه كفك لتحفظه لم يحصل فيه شيء فكذلك الدنيا

ITQAN:v3p146/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r1.speaker: الشيخ بهاء الدين
ITQAN:v3p146/r1.claim: Bahāʾ al-Dīn distinguishes ellipsis, where a short expression is part of a longer one, from concision, where few words convey a longer meaning.
ITQAN:v3p146/r1.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين الكلام القليل إن كان بعضا من كلام أطول منه فهو إيجاز حذف وإن كان كلاما يعطي معنى أطول منه فهو إيجاز قصر

ITQAN:v3p146/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p146/r2.claim: Some define concision as multiplying meaning while reducing wording; another defines it as using fewer words than customary for the meaning.
ITQAN:v3p146/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم إيجاز القصر هو تكثير المعنى بتقليل اللفظ

ITQAN:v3p146/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p146/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p146/r3.claim: Concision is eloquent because it demonstrates mastery of expression, as the Prophet's saying that he was given comprehensive speech illustrates.
ITQAN:v3p146/r3.anchor: وسبب حسنه أنه يدل على التمكن في الفصاحة

ITQAN:v3p107/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p107/r1.speaker: الكواشي
ITQAN:v3p107/r1.claim: Al-Kawāshī says an imperative used like a declarative is more emphatic because it conveys obligation, as in the example of promising hospitality.
ITQAN:v3p107/r1.anchor: قال الكواشي في الآية الأولى الأمر بمعنى الخبر أبلغ من الخبر لتضمنه اللزوم

ITQAN:v3p107/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p107/r2.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
ITQAN:v3p107/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām explains the force of this construction by the imperative's sense of obligation, transferred to the declarative.
ITQAN:v3p107/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عبد السلام لأن الأمر للإيجاب فشبه الخبر به في إيجابه

ITQAN:v4p514#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r2.claim: A weak report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet called a new good deed after an old sin unusually quick and effective in seeking and reaching its goal.
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p514#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r3.claim: Abū Dharr reports that the Prophet advised following a bad deed with a good one to erase it, and identified lā ilāha illā Allāh as the best good deed.
ITQAN:v4p514#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج أحمد عن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله أوصني

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r1.claim: Al-Ṣanawbarī likens stretched arcs on a pond to extended eyebrows: stretching reduces their curvature, just as extending an eyebrow does.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r1.anchor: أراد ما يبدو في صفحة الماء من أشكال كأنصاف دوائر صغار

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r2.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz compares early raindrops on earth to hurried dots scattered across a book page, combining shape with movement.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r2.anchor: ومن لطيف ذلك أيضا أعنى الجمع بين الشكل وهيئه الحركة قول ابن المعتز يصف وقوع القطر على الأرض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r3.claim: Motion becomes a composite image when parts move in different directions; a wheel or arrow moves simply, while a page alternately closing and opening changes direction.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r3.anchor: كلما كان التفاوت في الجهات التى تتحرك أبعاض الجسم إليها أشد كان التركيب في هيئة المتحرك اكثر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā compares a ship tossed by waves to a young calf's irregular rising and falling; الرباح can mean a calf or, by another view, a monkey, and الكرع is rainwater.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p158/r4.anchor: الرباح الفصيل وقيل القرد والكرع ماء السماء شبه السفينة في انحدارها وارتفاعها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r1.claim: Poets compare a dark horse's bright forehead to a star or dawn and its body to night; Ibn al-Muʿtazz reverses the image, making dawn a horse's blaze.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r1.anchor: ثم يعكس فيشبه النجم أو الصبح بالغرة في الفرس كقول ابن المعتز

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r2.claim: Though comparing maidens' figures to cypresses is conventional, poets refresh the image by making cypresses resemble women; a poem also depicts trees leaning as if seeking an embrace.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r2.anchor: وتشبه الجوارى في قدودهن بالسرو تشبيها عاميا مبتذلا ثم إنهم قد جعلوا فيه الفرع أصلا فشبهوا السرو بهن

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r3.claim: In Ibn al-Muʿtazz's cypress image, branches first lean toward an embrace and then recoil; the return to uprightness is faster than the initial bend.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r3.anchor: راعى الحركتين حركة التهيؤ للدنو والعناق وحركة الرجوع إلى أصل الافتراق وأدى ما يكون في الحركة الثانية من سرعة زائدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r4.claim: A shy person withdraws faster than approaching; fear and embarrassment impel more strongly than hope, while approach allows deliberation and withdrawal is compelled.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r4.anchor: حركة من يدركه الخجل فيرتدع أسرع أبدا من حركته إذا هم بالدنو فإزعاج الخوف والوجل أبدا أقوى من إزعاج الرجاء والأمل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r5.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz figures festivity and delight through women, presenting wine circulated among companions in the hand of a lovely woman.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p181/r5.anchor: ومن تشبيه السرور بالنساء قول ابن المعتز

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r1.claim: Poets compare young women's breasts to pomegranates, and also reverse the comparison to describe a pomegranate as a maiden's breast.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r1.anchor: ثم يقلب فيشبه الرمان بالثدى كقول القائل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r2.claim: Clear streams resemble swords in the water's whiteness and gleam and in their elongated shape; poets also reverse the image, likening swords' strokes to streams.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p183/r2.anchor: وتشبه الجداول والأنهار بالسيوف يراد بياض الماء الصافي وبصيصه مع شكل الاستطالة الذي هو شكل السيف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r1.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz requires the bird to be clipped-winged: a fixed tent buffeted inside by wind moves like a bird whose restricted wings beat continuously and backward.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r1.anchor: فشرط في الطائر أن يكون مقصوصا وذلك قوله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r2.claim: A comparison cannot always be reversed: when one object is an established extreme in a quality, it serves as the measure for an uncertain object, not vice versa.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r2.anchor: أن يكون بين الشيئين تفاوت شديد في الوصف الذي لأجله يشبه ثم قصدت أن تلحق الناقص منهما بالزائد مبالغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p191/r3.claim: Al-Buḥturī's night-as-ink comparison is weak because ink is not an unsurpassed standard of blackness; the night itself is the better established measure.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r1.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz first compares the rose's redness to blushing, then imagines literal shame and invents its cause: the rose feels unworthy beside the superior narcissus.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r1.anchor: أنه عمل أولا على قلب طرفي التشبيه كما مضى في فصل التشبيهات فشبه حمرة الورد بحمرة الخجل ثم تناسى ذلك وخدع عنه نفسه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r2.claim: Abū Hilāl al-ʿAskarī imagines the violet boasting that it matches a maiden's cheek; asking its back exposes the claim and comically elevates the flower's status.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p247/r2.anchor: ومما هو خليق أن يوضع في منزلة هذه القطعة ويلحق بها في لطف الصنعة قول أبي هلال العسكري

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r1.claim: With two definite nouns under kāna, either may be called subject and the other predicate; this grammatical choice does not make all reversed clauses equivalent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r1.anchor: إذا اجتمع معرفتان كنت بالخيار في جعل أيهما شئت اسما والآخر خبرا كقولك : كان زيد أخاك ، وكان أخوك زيدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p149/r2.claim: Fronting can set exclusive focus; reversing “only musk is perfume” and related lines by Jarir and al-Mutanabbi changes the intended meaning.

DAMGHANI:v1p293/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r4.claim: Aṭrāf al-nahār means times at the ends of the day; for 11:114 the work gives dawn, noon, and afternoon, also noting dawn prayer.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r4.anchor: فوجه منها الاطراف اوقات النهار قوله سبحانه في سورة طه

DAMGHANI:v1p255/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r7.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean minor sins that good deeds remove; another verse speaks of overlooking them.
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r7.anchor: السيئات الصغائر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r1.claim: Al-sayyiʾāt are the opposite of good deeds.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense is associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r2.anchor: أحدها : الشرك . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ﴿ وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r3.claim: A second sense is punishment or the consequences of wrongdoing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r3.anchor: والثاني : العذاب . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الزمر : ﴿ فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا ﴾ ]

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r4.claim: A third sense is harm or misfortune, including the afflictions that pass away.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r4.anchor: والثالث : الضر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف : ﴿ وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات ﴾ ، وفي هود : ﴿ ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r5.claim: A fourth sense is evil or wicked schemes.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r5.anchor: والرابع : الشر ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمن : ﴿ فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r6.claim: A fifth sense is men having sex with men, as in the account of Lot's people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p362/r6.anchor: والخامس : إتيان الرجال . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود : ^ ( ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات )

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f1.claim: Sibawayh distinguishes conditional nouns and adverbs such as من، ما، أي، متى، أين and أنى from the particles إن، إذما; elsewhere, adding ما turns certain temporal or spatial forms into conditionals.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f1.anchor: فما يجازى به من الأسماء غير الظروف من وما وأيهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f2.claim: حيث alone is not conditional because the following clause completes it as a relative place phrase; حيثما becomes conditional when ما changes its construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f2.anchor: حيث أن يجازى بها أنك تقول حيث تكون أكون فتكون وصل لها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f4.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f4.claim: Al-Khalil says كيف تصنع أصنع is an awkward expression, not a conditional particle, though its meaning is conditional: however you act, I act.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f4.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن قوله كيف تصنع أصنع فقال هي مستكرهة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f5.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f5.claim: Al-Khalil distinguishes إذا from إن: إذا points to a known time, while إن is indefinite; poetic uses of إذا as a conditional particle are forced, and ordinary إذا ما is sound.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f5.anchor: وسألته عن إذا ما منعهم أن يجازوا بها فقال الفعل في إذا بمنزلته في إذ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f6.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f6.claim: Al-Khalil calls إن the mother of conditional particles because it always remains conditional, while other particles can become interrogative or lose conditional force.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f6.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن إن هي أم حروف الجزاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f7.claim: A conditional answer must be a verb or a clause introduced by فاء; و and ثم cannot introduce it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f7.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يكون جواب الجزاء إلا بفعل أو بالفاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f9.claim: A nominal answer such as إن تأتني أنا كريم is not acceptable in ordinary speech because it begins a new sentence without فاء or إذا; poets Hassan ibn Thabit and an al-Asadi poet use it by compulsion.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالجزاء)#481/f9.anchor: وسألته عن قوله إن تأتني أنا كريم
